narration: Before an electric iron, how did a garment become smooth? These two women are beating cloth on a low stone. The Korean practice is called dadeumijil. Washed and starched fabric was pounded to smooth its surface. Notice the wooden beaters, then the different angles of their arms. A clean white garment could carry hours of unseen work. A visitor might admire the clothing and wonder how people cared for it. Here, the picture makes that hidden routine visible. We cannot hear a rhythm, but their shared task lets us imagine one. The work is attributed to Uncho. From the TJ Kim Collection, look beyond the garment to the hands that made it ready.
